case study · 03 / 05

IntelliMoney

An expense platform that turns transaction patterns into a financial health score.

PythonReactFastAPIMongoDBscikit-learnNLP

Live project ↗　GitHub ↗

outcomes

TF-IDF text featuresLogistic Regression categoriserJWT authentication

problem

Spending data is difficult to act on when categories and summaries require manual work. IntelliMoney automates categorisation and brings the results into a budgeting workflow.

architecture

decisions · why · trade-offs

Automate categorisation with TF-IDF and Logistic Regression.

Text features provide a practical way to map expense descriptions to categories.

Trade-off accepted: Ambiguous descriptions still need user correction.

Keep financial services behind authenticated APIs.

Budget records are user-specific data.

Trade-off accepted: The frontend depends on token lifecycle handling.

Present scores through interactive dashboards.

Users need to inspect patterns rather than receive a single static score.

Trade-off accepted: The score remains a summary of the underlying transactions.

result

  • Built expense categorisation, budgeting, and personalised financial health scoring.
  • Added dashboards and secure FastAPI/MongoDB services.

if I kept going…

  • Add a correction loop to improve category quality.
  • Explain score movement alongside individual budget changes.
